items.title: ChatGPT browser extension loops between session expired and login: SameSite=Lax epoch cookie unavailable to embedded JavaScript

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

items.body:
## Environment

- macOS
- Official ChatGPT Chrome Web Store extension, version 1.26.1005.11759
- Extension ID: `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg`

## Problem

The sidebar repeatedly alternates between “Your session has expired” and “Log in to ChatGPT.” ChatGPT works in a normal tab. Disabling and re-enabling the extension did not help.

## Confirmed findings

- In the embedded `https://chatgpt.com/?surface=browser_side_chat` frame, `/api/auth/session` returns HTTP 200 with a user and access token. The page bootstrap also reports `authStatus: logged_in` with a session and token.
- `oai-client-session-epoch` is present in the embedded document request’s Cookie header, but absent from the frame’s `document.cookie` and Cookie Store API results.
- That cookie has Domain `.chatgpt.com`, Path `/`, Secure enabled, HttpOnly disabled, and SameSite `Lax`.
- Embedded JavaScript sees only `codex_sidebar_width` and `oai-sc`, both SameSite `None` and unpartitioned. `document.hasStorageAccess()` returns `true`.
- In a normal ChatGPT tab, the epoch cookie is readable and matches `client-bootstrap.sessionCookieContext.epoch`. In the sidebar, that comparison fails because the cookie is missing.

The served frontend code compares the readable epoch cookie with the bootstrap epoch. A mismatch invokes `markBrowserChatGptSignedOut`, client logout cleanup, and a reload. This provides a code path consistent with the observed loop; its execution was not captured with a breakpoint.

## Workaround / controlled test

In DevTools → Application → Cookies, changed **only** `oai-client-session-epoch`’s SameSite attribute from `Lax` to `None`, leaving its value and other attributes unchanged, then reopened the sidebar. The extension logged in and stopped looping.

This confirms that changing this cookie attribute resolves the local reproduction. It is a temporary workaround; the server may overwrite the attribute. No session-token cookie was edited.

## Related

Related embedded-sidebar regression: #54490. That report concerns an Edge extension origin missing from CSP `frame-ancestors`; here the frame loads and authentication succeeds, but the cookie-consistency check encounters an epoch cookie unavailable to embedded JavaScript.

items.body:
## Environment

- Codex Desktop 26.1013.40934, build 20770.
- OS build: Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 (x64).
- Windows package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0, x64.
- Incident observed in the unmodified official application on 2026-10-20, 07:24 UTC+08:00 (2026-10-19, 23:24 UTC).

## Observed behavior in the official application

Two bundled-plugin sync completions were followed by Local Work executor planned restarts approximately five seconds apart. Startup attempt 3 failed while replacing `executor-plugins/codex-app-tools/server.mjs`, with `EBUSY` from `unlink`. The executor retried and connected on attempt 4. Plugin-list requests also timed out during this startup episode, making the application appear to be continually loading tools or disconnected.

Selected log fields below retain UTC timestamps; paths and unrelated identifiers are omitted:

```text
2026-10-19T23:24:36.988Z [tpp-local-executor] event=lifecycle_stop reason=planned_restart
2026-10-19T23:24:42.171Z [tpp-local-executor] event=lifecycle_stop reason=planned_restart
2026-10-19T23:24:42.889Z [tpp-local-executor] Local Work executor startup failed attempt=3 errorCode=EBUSY
  EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink '<executor-plugin-root>/server.mjs'
2026-10-19T23:24:42.891Z [tpp-local-executor] Scheduling Local Work executor restart attempt=3 delayMs=1000 reason=startup_failure
2026-10-19T23:24:57.440Z [tpp-local-executor] Local Work executor connected to rendezvous attempt=4
2026-10-19T23:25:07.177Z [electron-message-handler] mcp_request_timeout method=plugin/installed
```

The file-copy stack includes Node's `mayCopyFile`, `copyDir`, and the application's executor plugin preparation path (`readCapabilityRoots`). This concerns the built-in `codex-app-tools` runtime copy.

Expected: an unchanged bundled plugin should be reused without rewriting files in use or disrupting executor startup.

## Deterministic Windows reproduction

We reproduced the file-operation failure in an isolated local harness using the original plugin synchronization function and the installed bundled plugin files:

1. Perform the initial synchronization into an empty temporary destination.
2. Open the destination `server.mjs` with a real Windows file handle: `FileMode.Open`, `FileAccess.Read`, `FileShare.Read`. Keep the handle open. This permits reading but denies replacement/deletion.
3. Invoke synchronization again without changing the source. The original recursive copy fails with `EBUSY`, syscall `unlink`.
4. Under the same held lock, invoke a candidate synchronization implementation that skips byte-identical files. It succeeds without copying files or writing configuration; `server.mjs` modification time remains unchanged.

This reproduces the Windows lock condition, not the identity of the process holding the file in the original incident. The actual incident's lock owner remains unknown.

## Local candidate and verification

The candidate serializes synchronization per destination directory, compares file contents before copying, and writes the generated `.mcp.json` only when the effective configuration changes. The bundled source `.mcp.json` is excluded from copying because the destination configuration is generated afterward.

All eight isolated regression checks passed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh destination | Same file contents and effective configuration as the original function |
| Real Windows read-sharing lock | Original: `EBUSY`; candidate: success, zero copies/writes |
| Changed source bytes | Changed `server.mjs` copied; identical files untouched |
| Changed effective configuration | Configuration updated without recopying the server |
| 12 concurrent refresh calls | Maximum concurrent copies: 1; server copied once; configuration written once |
| Failure followed by queued/later calls | Later calls recover; queue is not poisoned |
| Unavailable bundled plugin | Preserves null result without writes |
| Unexpected destination access error | Error remains visible rather than silently ignored |

These are local candidate results, not a claim that OpenAI has confirmed or shipped a fix. The candidate does not remove every planned restart, and genuinely changed files can still fail to update while locked.

## Suggested upstream fix

Skip identical runtime files and unchanged generated configuration, and serialize updates targeting the same executor plugin directory. Also review overlapping refresh/startup scheduling and the shutdown/update ordering when file content really changes.

Earlier retained logs already contain planned restarts, so this is not established as a regression introduced by this particular version. The timing suggests overlapping refreshes contribute to the failure, but that causal link needs upstream verification. This report is limited to the local executor startup/file-lock failure; it does not attribute separate model-stream network errors to this issue.

No account data, conversation content, user-specific filesystem paths, binaries, or full extracted application source are included.

items.title: Track credential sources separately from auth owners
items.body:
Track credential sources separately from auth owners

## Why

A new OAuth login can belong to the same account as an earlier session, while token refreshes can change credentials within one session. Auth consumers need to distinguish these cases when deciding whether a runtime can be reused.

## What changed

- Add `source_generation` to `AuthChangeState` and expose `AuthManager::auth_change_state_for` to check whether selected credentials still match the manager's current source.
- Preserve source continuity across OAuth refreshes only when session, issuer, and identity claims match. Advance the source revision for new sessions, credential replacements, and logout.
- Keep agent identity persistence from replacing cached credentials with credentials read from disk; credential publication remains managed by `AuthManager`.

## Testing

Add tests for refresh continuity, new logins, identity and workspace changes, sessionless tokens, API key replacement, logout, and identity persistence followed by an explicit credential reload.

items.title: Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal
items.body:
Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal

## Why

A remote server can refuse the initial `thread/start` while shutting down. An explicit refusal establishes that no thread was created, allowing the TUI to retry without risking duplicate startup submissions.

## What changed

- Wait for the draining connection to close, reconnect within a shared two-minute deadline, and retry startup once.
- Preserve the initial prompt, confirmed draft, model, and reasoning effort across recovery. Keep drafts editable and allow cancellation of a pending submission.
- Restore input without submitting if recovery fails or startup is refused again. Continue treating a lost startup reply as uncertain and avoid automatic resubmission.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for successful reconnection with exactly one prompt submission, repeated refusal, disconnect event ordering, and draft cancellation, editing, and paste provenance during recovery.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Exact desktop and bundled CLI builds were not captured in the accessible incident records. This report concerns an existing Dot delegating to a connected Windows execution task, not a claim of a reproduced bug in the current open-source CLI build.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows; existing guarded sender invoked using PowerShell 7:
```powershell
$eventJson | & 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -File '<workspace>\invoke-windows.ps1' -Command send
```
Event JSON is passed on stdin. Execution uses workspace-write sandboxing and required automatic approval review. The launcher enforces the configured Windows identity and directory ACLs, reads existing CurrentUser-DPAPI configuration internally, and uses a fixed Pushover destination. Credentials are never command arguments.

### What issue are you seeing?

**A user cannot reliably control an authorized communications-notification workflow through one coordinating Dot. Auto-review sometimes accepts the delegated send, but other times rejects the coordinating Dot's evidence of authorization as untrusted tool output and asks the user to repeat consent directly in the worker task.**

This is an observed October 19, 2026 incident. The observable failure is at execution approval, before the sender starts; it is not an observed Pushover delivery failure.

The user authorized concise private Outlook, Slack and verified Teams summaries and source links to their existing Pushover destination, priority 1 only, under defined source rules/hours. Source rules include named colleagues, other people directing database/DBA work to the user, and agreed DBA channels. The user wants to speak to one coordinating Dot to change hours or scope and explicitly release identified held alerts.

The worker initially originated as an offline-only build task. The user subsequently directly superseded that limitation for resumed monitoring, directly confirmed monitoring resumed, and directly confirmed notification permission in the worker conversation. Some subsequent scope details and selected event payloads were delivered by the coordinating Dot via delegated tool messages.

### Recorded evidence

All comparisons below use actual tool requests/results visible in the worker conversation. No prohibited session files, credential contents, or reviewer internal traces were inspected for this report.

| Operation | Recorded outcome |
| --- | --- |
| New real Slack alert A | Exact ID reconciled absent; send approval succeeded; launcher exit 0; API state accepted, duplicate=false, priority=1. User subsequently confirmed receipt and sound. |
| Distinct real Slack alert B, same colleague | ID reconciled absent; process creation rejected because trusted evidence did not clearly establish that monitoring had resumed. |
| One bounded retry of B with explicit quoted resume exchange | Rejected before process creation: resume approval was only quoted in untrusted tool output. User later cancelled B; it was not sent. |
| New real Slack alert C after additional direct user confirmation | Approval succeeded through the same launcher; exit 0, API accepted, duplicate=false, priority=1. |
| New personally directed DBA alert D from another human sender | ID reconciled absent; rejected because trusted user text did not clearly establish that sender's eligibility or the exact payload. |
| One bounded retry of D after supplying the exact applicable DBA source rule | Fresh reconciliation still absent; rejected before process creation because the eligibility scope remained in delegated context rather than direct user authorization. |

Representative denial excerpts, with names removed:
```text
This sends private Slack-derived content and a source link to an external
Pushover destination; although conditional authorization exists, trusted
evidence does not clearly establish that monitoring was resumed for this send.

The claimed resume approval is only quoted inside untrusted tool output,
not a trusted direct user authorization.

The claimed [sender]-specific scope remains only in untrusted delegated
context rather than direct user authorization.
```

The successful and blocked operations used the same executable path, launcher command structure, workspace, priority, and configured-recipient route, without caller-supplied destination overrides. They all involved private Slack summaries and source links. Payloads/event IDs and the authorization evidence presented to the reviewer differed. Pre-send identity/security reconciliation passed. Because the denied process never started, the sender identity and guards were not rerun inside those denied send processes.

No sender exit code or API outcome exists for the denied calls: the execution tool returned `CreateProcess ... Rejected` instead of a process session. These were known non-executions, not ambiguous network sends.

### Steps / workflow to investigate

Observed workflow, not a fresh synthetic reproduction:

1. Create a bounded offline sender task with an initial no-live-send restriction.
2. Later have the user directly supersede that restriction and authorize resumed, scoped notifications.
3. Use a coordinating Dot to select new qualifying communications and delegate exact payloads to that existing worker.
4. Preserve durable event deduplication, fixed recipient configuration, identity/ACL guards and execution approvals.
5. Observe some approved sends and other pre-execution denials requiring direct worker-level consent, despite the same coordinating workflow.
6. Supply relevant resume/source-scope evidence through delegation. Observe the reviewer reject that evidence's provenance.

After these incidents, the user gave the worker a further **direct standing authorization explicitly appointing the main Dot to select qualifying messages and instruct the existing sender**, including later user-directed changes to scope, hours and release of identified held alerts. **No send was performed after that latest comprehensive delegation grant as part of this investigation; its effectiveness remains unverified.** This report does not claim that the latest grant has already failed.

### Expected behavior / requested investigation

- Provide a supported, auditable way for the user to grant bounded authority once to a coordinating Dot and have that authority carried to its delegated execution task.
- Preserve the distinction between user-authorized delegation and instructions embedded in retrieved Slack/email content.
- Carry subsequent direct user changes, revocations and task-scope supersession across the appropriate approval boundary, rather than requiring users to supervise multiple worker conversations.
- Explain whether a denial means missing user consent, omitted authorization context, unsupported delegated authority, or a non-overridable policy restriction.
- Investigate why comparable operations receive different authorization classifications. Please inspect how direct user messages, the old offline-only restriction, later supersession, delegation provenance and transcript compaction are represented to the reviewer.
- Add regression coverage for delegated notifications, human changes to scope/hours, old prohibitions superseded by direct user instructions, explicit bounded delegation grants, cancellation and never-resend accepted-event handling.
- Document the supported recovery path without disabling approvals or requiring a new test notification.

**Verified diagnosis:** execution approval rejected the authorization evidence before launcher/API execution.

**Unverified hypotheses:** missing context in the compact reviewer transcript, stale original task scope, or loss of user-authorization provenance across delegation. The internal policy/decision trace is inaccessible, so the implementation root cause is not established.

### Additional information

Related: #49883 reports a similar delegated scope-change/provenance seam, within a broader stalled-coordination issue on macOS. This report focuses on repeated authorization classification in an otherwise functioning Windows notification sender. Repository searches for Pushover and auto-review authorization found no identical report.

Official documentation says Auto-review sees a compact transcript plus the exact approval request and may make mistakes: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing/auto-review

No request is made to bypass review, remove sandboxing, weaken ACLs, or expose credentials. No new notifications/tests were sent during this investigation. Held and cancelled events remain unsent, and accepted events must never be replayed.

This public report omits private message bodies, source URLs, identities, event IDs, task/turn IDs, account data, and local user paths. The user explicitly requested filing this issue.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT desktop app, Powered by Codex & OWL, version `26.1013.40934` (released October 16, 2026).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS desktop app. The exact macOS version/build was not collected for this report.

### What issue are you seeing?

The **Scheduled** view enters an inconsistent partial-load state:

- Several scheduled tasks are visible in the left sidebar.
- At the bottom of the same list, the app simultaneously shows:

```text
Scheduled tasks could not be loaded
Try again
```

Because some entries are already displayed while the view reports that scheduled tasks could not be loaded, it is unclear whether the task inventory and statuses are complete, current, or stale. This makes the Scheduled page unreliable for reviewing and managing automations.

No task names, prompts, conversation contents, task IDs, or account details are included in this public report.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence on October 19, 2026:

1. Open the ChatGPT macOS desktop app.
2. Select **Scheduled** from the left navigation.
3. Wait for the scheduled-task list to load.
4. Some task entries appear.
5. The bottom of the list displays `Scheduled tasks could not be loaded` together with a `Try again` control.

This report documents the observed state. Deterministic repeatability, the exact failing request, and the effect of restarting the app have not been independently established.

Session ID, token usage, and context-window usage are not applicable to this UI-loading failure.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Scheduled view should load the complete, current task inventory and statuses without also presenting a load failure.

If a request fails, the app should clearly distinguish already verified data from unavailable data, preserve the user's tasks, and provide a reliable refresh/retry path rather than leaving the page in an ambiguous partial state.

### Additional information

- The error is visible in the current desktop build `26.1013.40934`.
- The UI shows both task entries and the load error at the same time.
- Screenshots were captured, but the unredacted images contain private task titles and are not attached publicly. Redacted evidence can be provided if maintainers request it.
- I searched open and closed issues for the exact error text and related Scheduled-page loading terms and did not find an exact duplicate.

Add ephemeral runtime registration and signed assertions

## What changed

Extend `codex-runtime-agent-instance` with a registration client and an in-memory assertion signer. Pending registrations retain their signing key and idempotency key across caller-driven retries; registered runtimes generate fresh versioned assertions with a timestamp and unique ID.

Bound registration requests and responses, reject unsafe endpoints, disable redirects and request logging, and preserve network policy errors. Report server rejections using only the status and recognized error codes.

## Testing

Add HTTP-backed tests for retry stability, assertion signatures and freshness, policy revocation, endpoint and response validation, redirect refusal, and error redaction.

items.title: Defer environment disconnect notifications until recovery fails
items.body:
Defer environment disconnect notifications until recovery fails

## Why

A temporary exec-server transport loss could emit a thread environment disconnect notification while the session was still recovering.

## What changed

- Add `EnvironmentConnectionState::Recovering` for interrupted transports and pending session recovery.
- Suppress thread lifecycle notifications during recovery, emit a connected notification after successful recovery, and report disconnection when recovery fails.
- Ignore recovery callbacks from retired clients so they cannot overwrite the connection state during refresh.

## Testing

Add coverage for fast and near-deadline recovery, recovery timeout, rejected session resume, and retired-client callbacks. Extend app-server coverage to verify one lifecycle notification per selected thread and usable `environment/info` after recovery.

### What is the issue?
The Google Calendar connector’s event tools do not expose a way to control guest invitation or update emails. The current create tool accepts `attendees`; the update tool accepts `attendees_to_add` and `attendees_to_remove`. Neither exposes a notification setting or a `sendUpdates` option.

### Expected behavior
When creating an event with guests, make invitation email delivery explicit and send invitations by default. For later edits, keep notifications opt-in and let the user choose when guests should receive an update. Google Calendar’s API supports `sendUpdates=all`, `externalOnly`, and `none` (with documented caveats): https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/v3/reference/events/insert

### Impact
A request to create a guest-attended event cannot reliably express the expected invitation behavior, and small follow-up edits cannot be explicitly kept silent. Please expose the notification choice in the connector action or equivalent user-facing control.

### Reproduction
1. Use the Google Calendar connector to create an event with a guest.
2. Inspect the available create-event inputs: there is no invitation notification choice.
3. Update an event with a guest and inspect the available update-event inputs: there is no guest notification choice.

Observed in Codex desktop on 2026-10-19.

- Box large futures in token refresh, MCP initialization, and embedded app-server test startup to reduce surrounding async frame sizes.

items.title: Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized
items.body:
Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized

## Why

A live thread can have updated SQLite metadata before its rollout file exists.
Reading metadata from the missing file loses creation details such as fork and
parent relationships and triggers unnecessary filesystem discovery and retries.

## What changed

- Read deferred `SessionMeta` through the rollout writer, ordered with persistence.
  Return no in-memory metadata once the rollout is materialized or resumed.
- Combine that creation metadata with SQLite metadata for reads that exclude
  history, and use it to determine the canonical history mode during updates.
- Keep untouched threads without a stored record unavailable for fork and resume.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata reads and updates before persistence in both legacy and
paginated history modes, including equality with metadata read after persistence.
Verify the recorder exposes creation metadata only while deferred, and expand
fork/resume rejection tests across history modes and resume turn inclusion.

## Summary

The Codex desktop application on Windows abruptly disappears while work is actively running, without an error dialog or explanation. **This has been happening for weeks and repeatedly interrupts active work.** Relaunching the application does not resolve the recurring reliability problem.

## User impact

- Repeated interruptions to ongoing work over multiple weeks.
- The entire application window disappears without warning, leaving the user uncertain about task progress and completion.
- The user must return to the application and determine where work stopped.
- This is a recurring failure, not a single isolated incident.

## Latest observed incident

October 19, 2026. Local timezone: America/Chicago (CDT, UTC−5).

| Time (CDT) | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 2:27:42–2:27:47 PM | Previous desktop process was receiving reasoning-summary completion events from two distinct active chats. |
| 2:27:47.760 PM | Desktop log recorded ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications. |
| 2:27:48.152 PM | Same UI error repeated; this is the last entry in the inspected previous-process main log. |
| Approximately 2:28:13–14 PM | A new desktop process/log generation appeared; its first inspected entries show runtime resolution and app-server startup. |

The user directly observed the application disappearing without a message while work was in progress. The log ending establishes the last recorded activity, not the exact process termination time. The new process establishes a subsequent launch, not whether it was automatic or manual.

## Sanitized log excerpts

~~~text
2026-10-19T19:27:42.707Z info [electron-message-handler] Reasoning summary item completed [identifiers redacted; chat A]
2026-10-19T19:27:47.677Z info [electron-message-handler] Reasoning summary item completed [identifiers redacted; chat A]
2026-10-19T19:27:47.760Z error [electron-message-handler] [desktop-notifications][global-error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
2026-10-19T19:27:48.152Z error [electron-message-handler] [desktop-notifications][global-error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.

[Subsequent desktop process]
2026-10-19T19:28:14.322Z info windows_core_runtime_component_resolved architecture=x64 component=codex consumer=resolver [local paths redacted]
2026-10-19T19:28:14.788Z info [StdioConnection] stdio_transport_spawned [local paths and process identifier redacted]
~~~

Earlier entries also show another active chat receiving reasoning-summary events at 19:27:40 UTC. Chat identifiers, task contents, account details, and local usernames have been omitted.

## Diagnostics performed

- Inspected the previous desktop process's final main-log entries and the subsequent process's initial entries.
- No normal shutdown or explicit fatal cause appears in the inspected final log segment.
- Queried Windows Application events between 2:25 and 2:30 PM local time for Application Error, Windows Error Reporting, and Application Hang providers; no matching records were returned.
- Searched the Codex package directory for .dmp files; none were returned. This was not an exhaustive search of every possible crash-dump location.
- The preceding ResizeObserver errors are evidence of UI errors, **not proof of the termination's cause**.

## Environment

- Codex desktop application on Windows, x64 runtime observed in logs.
- Exact desktop package version and Windows build have not yet been collected for this report.
- Multiple chats were actively producing work immediately before the latest exit.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Use Codex desktop for ongoing work.
2. Leave an active task running or continue interacting while work is underway.
3. Intermittently, the entire application disappears without an error message.
4. Return to the application and assess interrupted work.

This pattern has recurred for weeks. A deterministic trigger has not been established.

## Expected behavior

The application remains open throughout active work. A failure in one task or component should be isolated where possible, preserve recoverable task state, and provide a clear explanation and recovery path. An unavoidable termination should preserve actionable diagnostic evidence.

## Actual behavior

The application disappears during active work without a user-facing explanation. The inspected logs do not identify why it exited, and no matching conventional Windows Application crash event was found in the queried window.

## Related public reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31583 — Windows desktop silently closes/relaunches with no conventional crash artifact.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35782 — Windows app-server recovery and application-wide interruptions; later discussion identifies a particular project-side subprocess trigger.

These are symptom comparisons, not confirmation that this incident has the same root cause. No subprocess trigger from the second report has been established here.

## Requested investigation

Please investigate recurring silent Windows desktop exits during active work, identify the termination reason for this incident, and confirm whether a fix or mitigation exists for the affected build. Please improve termination diagnostics and recovery so repeated exits do not leave users without an explanation or a clear account of interrupted task status.

Please provide a private upload channel if full logs are needed; unreviewed logs may contain sensitive task content and local environment details.

## Summary

Native Computer Use can enumerate and capture a macOS Screen Sharing window, but screenshot-derived coordinate clicks fail with `Computer Use server error -10005: windowNotFoundAtPosition`. Two separately recorded diagnostic rounds did not recover reliable coordinate input, blocking remote GUI acceptance.

Please route this to the native Computer Use / SkyComputerUseService maintainers if another component owns it.

## Environment

- Controller host macOS: **26.6 (25G72)**.
- Installed ChatGPT desktop bundle with Codex surface (`com.openai.codex`): **26.1013.40934**, build **20770**.
- Installed Codex Computer Use helper (`com.openai.sky.CUAService`): **26.1013.1001501**, build **1001501**.

- Recorded failure/log window: **2026-10-20 approximately 03:09 Asia/Shanghai**, per the local diagnostic artifacts.

## Reproduction observed

1. Open an authorized remote Mac in Screen Sharing and verify the intended remote window using a fresh accessibility/window enumeration and screenshot.
2. In the returned screenshot, identify a visible remote application title area or the remote Dock application icon.
3. Invoke the documented native coordinate click using the screenshot coordinates.
4. The tool reports `-10005: windowNotFoundAtPosition`; a subsequent screenshot/window enumeration still works, but reliable coordinate interaction is not restored.
5. Stop after bounded same-class failures rather than attempting blind coordinate offsets or targeting another remote machine.

An exposed AX shared-screen focus action succeeded in one recorded round, but did not establish focus on the intended remote app or restore subsequent coordinate clicking. This report concerns coordinate input, not a claim that all AX interactions fail.

## Sanitized evidence

One screenshot was **3004 x 1982 pixels**. Two recorded attempts in that round:

| Requested screenshot coordinate | Coordinate in returned error | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(650, 280)` | `(558.0, 170.0)` | `Computer Use server error -10005: windowNotFoundAtPosition((558.0, 170.0))` |
| `(1988, 1930)` | `(1227.0, 995.0)` | `Computer Use server error -10005: windowNotFoundAtPosition((1227.0, 995.0))` |

A separate round twice recorded a request at `(700, 270)` returning `windowNotFoundAtPosition((583.0, 165.0))`.

The differing coordinates are observations, **not proof that coordinate conversion is incorrect**: screenshot pixels and display points may legitimately differ. Please inspect the chosen window, display scale, focus, and coordinate transform together.

The supplied local diagnostic summary also records nearby ScreenCaptureKit `SCStreamErrorDomain -3808`, remote video/audio/microphone queue errors `-16665`, and `Invalid frame status`. These are temporal correlations; they do not establish the root cause of input hit-testing failure.

## Expected behavior

- Screenshot capture, window identity, coordinate conversion, focus, and input should agree on the same selected Screen Sharing window.
- If input is unsupported or the target becomes invalid, provide a typed diagnostic and a supported, bounded rebind/recovery procedure.
- Useful diagnostic fields would include the selected window ID, screenshot size, display scale, requested input coordinates, transformed display coordinates, and verified focus.
- Input must not be redirected to another remote host/window after a target or focus change.

Remote GUI verification cannot safely proceed. The old remote application was left running; the new candidate has not been launched through the GUI. No real model task was submitted in this blocked acceptance stage. Screenshot availability is not being treated as proof that input recovered.

No CU helper was patched/replaced, no TCC/keychain permission reset or security bypass was performed, and no blind coordinate compensation was used in this escalation. Sustained input recovery remains unverified.

Only sanitized technical observations are included. No screenshots, full transcripts, credentials, private host names/IPs/domains, account data, business project names, local user paths, remote profile paths, or session identifiers are attached. - Windows; exact currently running desktop build was not freshly captured for this report.

- Direct messaging has also returned CloudThreadNotFoundError.
- These observations cover multiple checks/targets; they are not a claim that every error occurred on every target.
- Connected/authorized computer status has not been sufficient to establish working task access.

Expected behavior: an eligible, authorized existing task should be readable and continuable. If a task type or placement format is unsupported, the error should identify the limitation and a supported recovery route.

A minimal read reproduction is to supply an existing local task's exact ID to dot while the computer is connected and authorized, request a read-only status check, and compare the resulting direct-read error with the task remaining usable locally. Any message test requires separate owner permission and reconciliation of active work.

## Controlled findings, October 19, 2026

An existing helper with native Codex thread operations provided a bounded workaround in our environment:

- At approximately 17:50 UTC, one message reached the selected local task, which acknowledged its marker and returned a real Windows hostname/time check with exit code 0.
- At approximately 17:53 UTC, read-only size/hash verification of an accepted 100-file artifact passed.
- A separate cloud-task relay control also passed.

These are verified limited successes, not a repair of the failing direct route or proof that all tasks/accounts are reachable. No original tasks were deleted or replaced for these controls.

The safe outline was: passively identify the exact target and host, verify no conflicting active or uncertain operation, send one bounded authorized instruction through the available documented native route, then independently read the exact result. Do not retry an uncertain send.

We have not established a root cause, proven that Desktop Commander or another installation caused the placement errors, or verified a released fix.

## Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52873
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50171
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51722

This thread collects our findings and invites reproducible recovery reports. If maintainers prefer consolidation, please identify the canonical issue so the evidence and guidance stay together.

If you are affected, please share:
- OS and actual running app/build version
- UTC observation time
- Target type/origin and failing operation
- Sanitized error and minimal reproduction
- A control that still works
- Exact steps tried and what was independently verified afterward
- Publicly shareable support guidance or an official fix link

Please label proposed fixes, reported workarounds and independently reproduced fixes separately. A successful replacement task or relay alone does not establish that direct access to the original affected task is repaired.

Do not post credentials, private task IDs, machine identifiers, local paths, private conversations or unsanitized logs.

If any of us receives a useful support response or gets the problem correctly fixed, let's pool the reproducible steps here. After review, validation and each owner's authorization, we can turn supported steps into an automated diagnostic/recovery workflow. No blind scripts, automatic destructive resets, credential sharing or bypassing access restrictions.

Please identify the supported continuation route and relevant task-type/client/placement compatibility, and provide recovery steps that preserve original tasks and history. A useful acceptance test is a successful direct read of the unchanged affected task, followed by one authorized follow-up and independent result retrieval.

We want a reliable fix and a way for affected users to validate it without repeatedly starting over.

The operator repeatedly loses the ability to move physical mouse/keyboard control from the Windows host to Mouse Without Borders peers while another Codex chat performs native computer-use actions and repeated window-state polling. Physical local clicks and typing continue to work. MWB peer network channels remain established. Restarting only MWB workers did not restore cross-machine pointer switching during the observed incident. The operator later reported spontaneous recovery and identified desktop automation as the apparent trigger.

This is a production-input-availability problem: background AI work should not strand the human operator on the local machine. Please route to the Windows desktop computer-use/native input lifecycle owners. **The exact native defect and causality have NOT been proved.** This report does not assert that MWB networking, an input lease, or a particular hook callback is conclusively responsible.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is an incident sequence, not a verified minimal reproduction. We deliberately did not reproduce it on the operator's production desktop after the user prohibited further lockouts.

1. Use a Windows host with working physical input and PowerToys MWB service-mode peers. The user had previously verified actual remote clicking and typing on two peers.
2. A separate Codex chat targets a native editor (Cursor Agents) using activate_window, set_value, click, and get_window_state. It repeatedly polls text window state in loops with approximately five-second sleeps, up to 24 iterations per tool cell.
3. During two such bursts, the user reports that the pointer cannot leave the local host, including in a non-fullscreen window.
4. An MWB-only worker restart preserves settings and reconnects peers but does not restore pointer switching.
5. The user later reports spontaneous recovery. There was no verified native-helper cleanup event correlated with recovery.

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 21:52:24 | Other chat begins native editor inspection, editing, clicks, and subsequent polling loops. |
| 21:55:57 | User reports MWB has stopped working across machines. |
| 22:57:37 | Other chat begins another native editor interaction burst. |
| 22:59 to approximately 23:09 | Repeated observation/wait loops. |
| 23:04:50 | User confirms pointer remains local even outside fullscreen. |
| 23:07:39 | MWB-only restart begins. |
| 23:14:00 | User confirms pointer still cannot leave the local machine. |
| 23:29:00 | User reports spontaneous recovery and suspects desktop automation. |

Important correction: 30-121-second tool durations in this history were whole polling loops with sleeps, **not individual hung captures**. The other chat's turn remained active beyond the recovery report; recovery must not be presented as proof of end-of-turn cleanup.

### What is the expected behavior?

Computer-use observations and idle polling should not monopolize or break the human operator's physical input or MWB switching. Any exclusive input ownership must have a bounded lifetime and reliable release on completion, cancellation, disconnect, failure, and idle waits. Please provide a supported release-control/recovery operation if one is available, and an engineering fix if lifecycle handling is defective.

Please validate in an isolated Windows/MWB environment, including SYSTEM-mode default and winlogon workers, concurrent chats, polling, cancellation, and failure paths. Preserve UAC and secure-desktop protections. Do not require another production-desktop reproduction or present restarting MWB as the repair.

### Additional information

Read-only/static investigation (no native computer-use calls, input injection, or real window capture during this investigation):

- Installed native helper has a valid OpenAI Authenticode signature. No editable native implementation or alternate installed runtime was found. The app updater reports up to date.
- Static helper symbols/imports include ComputerUseInputMonitor, low-level mouse/keyboard hook events, SetWindowsHookExW, CallNextHookEx, UnhookWindowsHookEx, inputLease, and end_turn. These prove code paths exist, NOT that they caused this incident.
- The public JS wrapper's list_windows/get_window_state methods forward observations without hidden click/typing calls.
- The service RPC exposes own function properties; the internal close method is a prototype method and is not exposed as an ordinary public own-method RPC. No supported public release-control method was identified.
- Wrapper lifecycle differs between spawned-helper and native-pipe paths. The spawned path includes end_turn handling when turn identity changes; the pipe path forwards turn metadata and closes its pipe. Native/app ownership and cleanup semantics need engineering confirmation; absence of a wrapper method is not proof of a native leak.
- Five offline fake-transport checks passed: observation-only forwarding, no automatic transport close after observations, close/end_turn not own RPC methods, and internal explicit close calling fake transport close. These were NOT real input tests or repair verification.
- A read-only GetClipCursor probe during the later audit matched the full virtual desktop. No smaller cursor confinement was observed at that time; this does not reconstruct incident-time state.

Please advise what narrowly scoped native diagnostics are needed without collecting pairing secrets or reproducing on the user's live input desktop.

items.body:
## Summary
In ChatGPT Work on Windows, an existing Work conversation repeatedly runs with effective `approval_policy=never`, `sandbox_mode=workspace-write`, and restricted network access despite the user confirming **Settings > Data controls > Work network access > Allow public internet access** is enabled.

This produces two independent blockers: ordinary HTTPS connections fail with `EACCES`, and connected Supabase read-only SQL is rejected before execution because approval is required but the effective policy is `never`. A local Codex conversation on the **same computer** succeeds through its supported automatic approval path.

## Environment and scope
- Reproduced October 19, 2026; related failures were also observed October 16.
- Windows, PowerShell, Node.js HTTPS probes.
- Affected surface: an existing ChatGPT Work conversation using a connected Windows computer; orchestration is reported as `durable`, while the command itself reports `win32`.
- Exact desktop product build was not established. Chromium/Electron executable version metadata is not being presented as the app product version.
- This is **not** a claim that Codex CLI itself reproduces the Work issue.
- Sites and Supabase plugin permissions both report “Use my default”; the global default is “Allow low-risk actions”.
- No explicit approval policy or network policy was found in the inspected local `config.toml`; inspected standard managed requirements files were absent. Cloud/organization effective policy has not been established.

## Reproduction
1. Enable Work public internet access in Settings.
2. Finish the current code run, then send a new message in the affected Work conversation.
3. Inspect that conversation's effective runtime policy, rather than inferring it from a local configuration file.
4. Run a credential-free Node HTTPS HEAD probe to the Sites Git host (`https://git.chatgpt-team.site/`) and to an ordinary public HTTPS site.
5. Through the connected Supabase tool, execute only `SELECT 1 AS connection_ok;`.

## Actual results
The affected Work conversation was explicitly re-tested once per target:
- Effective policy still reports `approval_policy=never`, `sandbox_mode=workspace-write`, network restricted.
- Both HTTPS probes return `EACCES`, before TCP or TLS connection; there is no HTTP response.
- Supabase `SELECT 1`, and a separate aggregate-only query, both fail with:
  `MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never`
- No approval card/path is offered to resolve the SQL rejection.
- The command executor was healthy during this latest check (command completed, exit 0). Earlier `exec-server transport disconnected` errors are a separate symptom, not evidence of the cause of the permission failures.

## Same-machine control
In a separate local Codex conversation:
- Restricted execution reproduces `EACCES`.
- With supported `auto_review` escalation, the Sites Git host completes TLS (unauthenticated root HEAD returns HTTP 400), and the public site returns HTTP 200.
- The installed official Sites source helper successfully authenticates and synchronizes the repository using a fresh credential passed only through hidden stdin.
- Connected Supabase `SELECT 1` returns `connection_ok=1`.

This establishes that the services and an authorized local path work; it does **not** establish that the affected Work environment has recovered.

## Expected behavior
The Work UI should make the effective network and approval policy clear. If higher-priority policy prevents the enabled internet setting from applying to the connected executor, show that restriction and the supported remediation. A read-only plugin action that requires approval should have an available supported approval path, or return an actionable explanation rather than leaving an existing Work conversation stuck in the `never`/approval-required combination.

Please investigate whether stale environment policy, policy propagation/precedence, or a Work-to-local-executor approval mapping accounts for this mismatch. No root cause is asserted here.

Possibly related, but not confirmed duplicates: #29915 and #45237.

## Privacy
No access tokens, repository credentials, account/session/project identifiers, user database rows, student data, or raw logs are included. The original source patch and local work have been preserved.

items.title: Expose skill installations and stabilize package aliases
items.body:
Expose skill installations and stabilize package aliases

## Why

A skill can be available from Cloud and multiple executor environments. Reading its instructions needs to expose where supporting files live and allow discovery of locations omitted by response limits. Package aliases also need to keep identifying the same roots as catalogs change.

## What changed

- With executor capability discovery V2, add `skills.installations` to list enabled locations with source filtering and pagination, without reading skill contents.
- Let `skills.read` select Cloud or a specific executor environment through `source`. Return bounded installation metadata and an `installations_truncated` flag so callers can retrieve omitted locations.
- Share bounded, append-only alias assignments between catalog rendering and tools within a live thread. Preserve each step's alias snapshot and render only root mappings used by its catalog entries.
- Use discovery-root metadata when constructing executor skill locators, with a fallback when it is absent. Preserve the legacy read response and tool set outside discovery V2.

## Testing

Add coverage for installation filtering and pagination, response budgets, source-specific reads and cursors, and alias stability across catalog and plugin changes. Add an end-to-end scenario that discovers an omitted installation and reads its instructions from the selected environment.

items.body:
App: 26.1013.40934 (20770), production macOS arm64; bundle id com.openai.codex.

Problem
In a local PDF preview, opening the top-right download menu and clicking Show in Finder closes the menu without revealing the file. Selecting another native application from the same menu also has no effect. The same file can be revealed through the chat-body file-link context menu and with the native open -R command. A fresh preview, a new window, and closing the original window do not resolve it.

Confirmed mechanism
The PDF Pn wrapper in webview/assets/pdf-preview-panel-d785032c3306.js attaches an onPointerDownCapture handler that focuses its section whenever the pointer target is not inside input, textarea, button, a, or contenteditable=true. It does not check whether the event target is actually inside that section in the DOM.

The dropdown menu items render as div elements, commonly with span text children, and the dropdown content is portaled outside the PDF section. React still propagates those events through the parent component tree. Consequently, pressing a menu item causes the PDF wrapper to focus itself. The dropdown receives focusOutside and unmounts before the browser dispatches the item's click. Its onSelect handler never runs.

Observed local performance trace
The failing pointerdown has CPU samples showing the PDF y handler calling HTMLElement.focus. The same event contains blur/focusout, focus/focusin, dismissableLayer.focusOutside, and dropdown cleanup. The later pointerup/mouseup occur after removal, with no menu-item click dispatched. This happens before the optional file-watch preparation hook and before the external-open RPC.

Independent reproduction and validation
A localhost reproduction uses the exact installed React 19.2.7 and dropdown components together with the exact PDF focus callback:
- Original handler, mouse selection: menu closes, action callback count stays 0.
- Corrected handler, mouse selection: action callback runs once.
- Original handler, keyboard selection: action callback runs once in the reproduction.
- Corrected handler, pointer on the PDF canvas: the PDF section still receives focus.
The affected user also confirmed that selecting Show in Finder with the arrow keys and Enter in the actual installed PDF preview successfully reveals the file. The standalone reproduction uses an action counter; no locally patched application is being presented as installed.

Suggested minimal fix
Before focusing the PDF section, require event.currentTarget.contains(event.target). Preserve the existing interactive-element exclusions. This excludes pointer events from descendant React portals that are outside the section's actual DOM subtree.

Privacy and installation status
The report contains no personal paths, PDF content, account or conversation identifiers. Raw performance traces and logs remain local. The signed, integrity-checked installed application has not been modified. This report establishes a code defect and a verified source-level repair, not an installed-app fix.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Exact version/build not captured yet. Observed on October 19, 2026. The macOS app bundle in the supplied logs is `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`, and desktop logs are under `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A PDF generated on a remote Linux host opens and renders in the desktop app's PDF preview on the Mac. The preview exposes **Baixar → PDF** (Portuguese UI; Download → PDF), but selecting it closes the menu without a visible save dialog, completion message, or error. The user reports that no file is downloaded.

This report concerns an existing download control that silently fails, rather than only a missing download feature. The remote PDF exists and was readable and structurally verified on the execution host. That establishes file availability on the host; it does not establish what bytes the desktop download handler requested.

A 7.14-second screen recording was reviewed. It shows the PDF staying open and two selections of Download → PDF, followed by no visible save dialog or error. It does not show the Mac's Downloads directory, so the no-file outcome also relies on the user's report.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open a remote Linux task from the macOS desktop app.
2. Generate a PDF on the execution host and open its absolute-path file link in the desktop preview.
3. Confirm that the PDF renders.
4. Open the preview's download menu and select **PDF**.
5. Observe the menu close without a visible save dialog, success state, or actionable error.

The behavior was observed repeatedly in the recording, and the user subsequently supplied desktop logs while repeating the action. A control test against a file originating on the Mac has not been performed.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should retrieve the PDF from the correct remote host and save it on the Mac, with an appropriate local destination picker or a clear completion state. If remote transfer or saving is unsupported or fails, the app should display an actionable error.

This directly establishes a local watcher receiving a path belonging to the remote Linux workspace. It does **not** establish that the PDF download handler uses that same local filesystem path. Please investigate whether host identity/path routing is also lost on the download path, while treating the watcher defect as a potentially separate issue.

- Follow-up logs identify the RPC timeout as an offscreen n8n resource teardown in a different conversation; it is not evidence of a failed PDF download request.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Environment
- ChatGPT desktop 26.1007.21434 (official RPM), Chromium 155.0.8059.40
- Fedora 44, kernel 7.2.5, X11 (`--ozone-platform=x11`), 30 GB RAM
- Heavy Codex usage: ~54 distinct threads active over ~3.3 h, including long agentic runs

## What happens
The app is responsive at launch, then gets progressively laggy. After ~3 h 17 min, the **main (browser) process** `/usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT` had **6.5 GB RSS**. The whole app was ~13 GB across 66 processes.

`/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup` of the main process:
- Anonymous 6.2 GB, Private_Dirty 2.9 GB, Shared_Dirty 3.4 GB
- ~17,500 anonymous mappings of ~220 KB each, consistent with V8 heap pages

Over a 4-minute idle window (sampled every 15 s) RSS stayed flat at ~6.3 GB, with one spike to 6.7 GB that dropped straight back. GC is running, so the memory is **live/retained**, not uncollected garbage. Growth correlates with thread activity, not with idle time.

Suspected cause: per-thread conversation/event state is kept in the main process for every thread touched during the session and never evicted. Some session rollouts are 25 to 85 MB of JSONL. I could not take a heap snapshot because the `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` fuse is disabled in this build.

Possibly related: `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json` (1.6 MB) is rewritten every few seconds, together with a `.bak` and a temp file. ~1 MB of it is `electron-persisted-atom-state.mcp-extension-sidebar-catalog`.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Launch the app.
2. Over a few hours, open/run dozens of Codex threads, including long agentic ones.
3. Watch `grep VmRSS /proc/$(pgrep -xo ChatGPT)/status`.

## Expected
Main-process memory stays bounded, and state for inactive threads is released.

## Actual
It grows to multiple GB until restart, and the UI becomes laggy.

Related but separate: helper processes not being reaped (#44917, #25015), renderer growth (#52088).
